clue.text: Initial payment bound to include bribe in return

indicators.note: to include means the word for bound wraps around the word for bribe
in return asks for the whole combined string to be turned round and read the other way

blocks.note: bound, as with rope, is tied
a sop is something given to pacify or buy someone off

explanation.surface: A first instalment comes with a kickback attached, paid back in kind.
explanation.walkthrough: TI(SOP)ED is built first, then the whole thing is read backwards to give DEPOSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is the sum handed over first to secure a purchase, with the balance paid later.

clue.text: Boil for two months

explanation.surface: Simmer something for two whole months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two months' reads as a duration; it actually supplies two month abbreviations, DEC and OCT.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoct is to boil a substance down to extract its essence, as in making a decoction.

clue.text: Reduce books in relation

blocks.note: to pare is to trim down

explanation.surface: Cutting down on reading matter about kinship.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent is a mother or father, a close family member and so a relation.

clue.text: Group sharing 'usband complain about hearty dish

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in this word tells you to drop the H from the group too
about means the complaint word goes round the group

blocks.note: the wives of one man, who share him
to squeal is to protest loudly

explanation.surface: A cockney wife grumbles that the household shares a husband over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'usband mimics a dropped aitch, so the group of wives loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: A square meal is a substantial, nourishing meal, which is what a hearty dish provides.

clue.text: Everything in Plato turned round

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow
round means the found letters are turned about to read the other way

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: All of Plato's thought, turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the whole amount, everything added together.

clue.text: Rub up, if given brush-off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Polish something up, if you get given the brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush-off' reads as a snub, but the hyphen hides the word brush followed by its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To furbish is to polish or burnish, restoring the shine of something by rubbing it.

clue.text: Anticipate a lot of trees - 4?

blocks.note: a forest is a large area of trees
the answer to 4 down means everything, which is all

explanation.surface: Predicting a huge number of trees, with a nod to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference uses the answer to 4 down, everything, as a synonym rather than as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act ahead of an event so as to prevent it, getting in first.

clue.text: Be rewarded with dialectal river in posh accent

indicators.note: in places the river word inside the abbreviation for the accent

blocks.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.surface: Getting one's reward by speaking of a river in a plummy voice.
explanation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the accent associated with the BBC and public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to gather in a harvest, and figuratively to receive the benefits of one's efforts.

clue.text: Bad reversal of northern light for Orsino and Olivia, say

definitions.note: an adjective describing them, not a synonym for them

indicators.note: reversal of says the following words' letters run the opposite way

explanation.surface: A sad turn for the northern lights, seen by two Shakespearean lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino and Olivia live in Illyria, the setting of Twelfth Night; the 'northern light' phrase hides N and a word for light.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino and Olivia, from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, are natives of Illyria on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Remnant to be suspended round middle of range

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letters, dropping both ends
round means the suspended word goes outside the kept letters

blocks.note: range without its first and last letters
to hover is to hang in the air

explanation.surface: What is left over after hanging around in the middle of a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is something surviving from an earlier time, a leftover or relic.

clue.text: Isle of Gold first formed in copper

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word formed
in places the preceding letters inside the symbol for copper

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An island of gold was first shaped inside copper, like a myth of creation.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, off the coast of Albania.

clue.text: Covering prolific corres-pondent in train crash

indicators.note: a crashed train is a wreck, so its letters lie scrambled
in puts the correspondent inside the wrecked word

blocks.note: St Paul wrote many of the New Testament epistles

explanation.surface: A busy letter-writer is caught up in a rail accident, ending under a sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in corres-pondent is a quirk of the source's typesetting; the phrase means a writer of many letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproof sheet used to cover loads, boats or goods.

clue.text: Interlaces components, as bureaucracy may?

indicators.note: the components of a word are its letters, taken apart and put together afresh

explanation.surface: Weaving parts together, the way an administrative machine tends to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of action rather than a synonym, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucracies tend to gather power and control into one central office, which is what centralising does.

clue.text: Flower of Conrad's "Heart" read backwards

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its inside, dropping the first and last letters
read backwards says the kept letters run right to left

blocks.note: the inner letters of Conrad, with C and D dropped

explanation.surface: Conrad's Heart of Darkness is a book about a river journey, read here backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, something that flows; the Arno runs through Florence and Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, hence a 'flow-er', and the Arno is an Italian river.

clue.text: Actress (not West) to grow out of terrorist costume

indicators.note: not West means losing the compass letter for west, while hinting it is not Mae West
out of means sitting outside, around the next words

blocks.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group

explanation.surface: An actress, not Mae West, outgrows her terrorist disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket does double duty: the actress is not Mae West, and W is removed from grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Unfortunate outcome is about to disrupt the union

indicators.note: to disrupt means breaking into the union and lodging in its middle

blocks.note: c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A sad result is about to break up a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscarriage, as in a miscarriage of justice, is a failure or a result that goes badly wrong.

clue.text: Pretend to keep time and get going

indicators.note: to keep means holding the time letter inside

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Fake keeping the beat, then get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To stimulate is to rouse into action, to set something going or spur it on.

clue.text: Turn up prompt (after one) for decoration

indicators.note: after places the prompt word behind the numeral

blocks.note: to curl is to turn upward
a cue is an actor's prompt

explanation.surface: Show up on time, after one o'clock, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A curlicue is an ornamental twist or flourish in handwriting or design.

clue.text: Surprises model kept in dark, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the dark word is dropped
kept in means the model sits inside the other word

explanation.surface: A model is held captive in darkness, much to everyone's shock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Henry Ford's famous car, so model gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give someone a sudden shock or fright, so startles means surprises.

clue.text: Posh officer has lots of pasta and in French is extremely colourful

definitions.note: jokey definition: beyond violet, at the extreme end of the spectrum

indicators.note: lots of, rather than all of, means the pasta loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A smart officer piles up pasta and turns out, in French style, very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old British usage made famous by Nancy Mitford.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultraviolet light lies past violet, beyond the visible spectrum, so it is colour taken to an extreme.

clue.text: Article on origin of language

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits on top of, so after, the second

blocks.note: the germ of an idea is its origin

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about where language comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: German is the tongue spoken in Germany, Austria and much of Switzerland.

clue.text: Storey designed with delicacy

indicators.note: designed means planned out anew, so the letters are given a new layout

explanation.surface: A floor of a building laid out with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicacy' looks like it describes the design's care, but it is a fine food.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are a shellfish prized as luxury food, a classic gourmet treat.

clue.text: Fun with bird

blocks.note: first meaning: a prank or bit of mischief
second meaning: a songbird famous for singing in flight

explanation.walkthrough: Fun with bird reads like slang for an evening out with a girlfriend; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for a lark means for fun, and the skylark is a common songbird.

clue.text: Encourage return into town, pursuing stench of cant

indicators.note: return means the word for encourage goes back the way it came
into puts those letters inside the town
pursuing places the town part after the stench part

blocks.note: a hum is a bad smell
to egg on is to urge
Bury is a town near Manchester

explanation.surface: Urging a return to town, following a smell of hypocrisy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hum for a stink is informal British usage; Bury is a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbuggery is hypocritical talk or sham, which is what cant means: insincere pious language.

clue.text: Approve of the second-rate and inferior

explanation.surface: Endorsing the mediocre and the poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless something is to give it one's sanction or consent.

clue.text: Victim in Cortez's adventure, initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letters of the words before it

blocks.note: first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone who suffered in the Spanish conquistador's expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: The conquest of Peru was Pizarro's, but the Incas were victims of the Spanish conquest generally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people were conquered and destroyed by Spanish invaders in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Columns put a stop to new dean

indicators.note: new means made over in a fresh form, so the letters of dean are rearranged

blocks.note: a colon is a punctuation mark, a stop

explanation.surface: Pillars put an end to the new dean's plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns, usually supporting a roof or entablature.

clue.text: Turn back the clock for reference

indicators.note: turn back says the clock word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Putting the clocks back, as a matter of record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn back the clock' suggests nostalgia; here it is literally a word read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is a body's terms of reference, the brief of what it is to consider.

clue.text: Being to wash and take into service

blocks.note: ens is a philosophical term for being or existence
lave is a literary verb for wash

explanation.surface: Someone who must wash and be put to work as a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ens, Latin for being, is a crossword staple from philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave someone is to force them into servitude, bound to work for another.

clue.text: Belgian artist back about one with consonant transposer

indicators.note: back means the artist's name is written in the other direction
about means those letters go round the number word

blocks.note: Felicien Rops was a Belgian printmaker

explanation.surface: A Belgian painter returns with a man who swaps letters round.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rev William Spooner of Oxford gave his name to the spoonerism, swapping the opening sounds of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooner was famed for transposing initial consonants, as in 'a well-boiled icicle' for a well-oiled bicycle.
